_comment: DOC-3. The operator guide, in the app rather than on GitHub. ONE copy: this file is the source, and the deploy copies it to the dashboard - exactly like stop-reasons.json and assessment-reasons.json. Never add a second copy under src/dashboard; a guard test fails if you do. Plain language, and it goes through the same no-jargon guard as every other operator-facing string. MANUAL-REVIEW-1: each entry says what the page shows, what each control does, and where to go next. Every fact is read from the page and the engine, and a step or a button is named by its label on the page.

index.html.title: Overview
index.html.what: The Overview shows what waits for a person, and what runs now. Nothing on this page changes a machine.
howToRead: Four tiles count the migrations that wait for a person or for approval, the migrations that run now, and the assessments to review.
Select a tile to show its list. The list shows 10 rows on each page.
Use Project and Search to find a migration or an assessment. Select its name to open it.
index.html.nextStep: Open a migration or an assessment that waits. If nothing waits, open the Projects page.

projects.html.title: Projects
projects.html.what: A project holds one estate: its assessments, and the migrations planned from them.
howToRead: Three tiles count all projects, the projects with a machine that waits for a person, and the projects with no change in 30 days.
Select a tile to show its list. The list shows 10 projects on each page. Use Sort and Search to find a project.
Each row shows how many assessments and migrations the project holds. Select a count to open them.
New project makes a project. New assessment starts an assessment in that project.
projects.html.nextStep: Create a project, then start an assessment in it. Nothing on this page changes a machine.

assessments.html.title: Assessments
assessments.html.what: An assessment reads your machines and changes nothing. It shows which machines can migrate, and what stops the other machines.
howToRead: Four tiles count the assessments to review, the accepted assessments with no migration, the assessments with a migration, and all assessments.
Select a tile to show its list. The list shows 10 assessments on each page. Select the name of an assessment to open its report.
The report groups the machines by each finding. Each card says what to do.
Select I have reviewed this to accept the assessment. A migration can only be planned from an accepted assessment.
assessments.html.nextStep: Accept the assessment, then select Plan a migration.

migrations.html.title: Migrations
migrations.html.what: A migration moves machines to their targets, one wave at a time. This page shows each wave, each machine, and the activity.
howToRead: A wave starts when a person starts it, or at its scheduled time. A wave can need an approval before it starts.
After you sign off the plan, the product starts each next wave when the wave before it ends. It waits while a machine waits for a person, or while the run is paused.
The activity list shows each step, newest first. A step that failed and then passed on a retry shows as recovered.
The product takes a safety copy of each machine before it changes the machine. If a machine fails its checks after the move, the product rolls it back from that copy.
The Quota and on-demand capacity reservations card shows the quota and the on-demand capacity reservation of each wave. Select Release to release one.
migrations.html.nextStep: Open a machine that waits for a person. Its panel shows the step it stopped at and what to do.

wizard.html.title: Assess and migrate
wizard.html.what: This page assesses an estate. Then it plans a migration from an accepted assessment.
howToRead: The assessment reads your machines and changes nothing. A person reviews it and accepts it.
Planning has five steps: Choose the machines, Choose each target, How to group them, Arrange the waves and Run it.
Choose each target shows the options of each machine. A machine can take only the options shown for it.
In Arrange the waves, select Check the quota and Reserve capacity before the wave starts. Azure accepts or refuses each quota increase request. The answer can come after some days.
wizard.html.nextStep: Of the planning steps, only Run it changes a machine. You can leave this page and open it again. The product keeps what each step saved.

reports.html.title: Reports
reports.html.what: Reports shows the result of each migration: which machines moved, the waves, the sign-offs and the issues.
howToRead: Five tiles count all migrations, the finished migrations, the migrations in progress, the migrations that need attention now, and the migrations with no plan.
Select a tile to show its list. The list shows 10 migrations on each page. Select the name of a migration to show its waves, sign-offs and issues.
A user with the Administrator role also sees Records to download, with the full record of each migration.
The Safety copies card shows the safety copies that the product keeps, and when the daily cleanup runs.
The engine builds the report when a wave ends and after a restore. The daily check builds it again when it is out of date.
reports.html.nextStep: Select Open the full report to read the report of a migration, or to download it.

access.html.title: Admin
access.html.what: The Admin page sets who can use the product, and where in Azure the product can work.
howToRead: Give each user or group a role: Viewer, Operator, Approver or Administrator.
Where the product may work gives the product access to a management group, a subscription or a resource group. You give it with your own Azure permissions.
Assess gives the VMF Assessment role, which reads and changes nothing. Assess and migrate gives the VMF Migration role.
access.html.nextStep: If a user cannot see a migration, check the role of the user here. Then check that the product has access to the subscription of the machines.

waves.html.title: Waves
waves.html.what: A wave is a group of machines that move together. The wave editor sets the machines and the settings of each wave.
howToRead: Move machines between waves, and set the settings of each wave.
Check the quota, on the card Request a quota increase, checks the quota of every wave of the plan. Reserve capacity makes an on-demand capacity reservation for the wave.
Save the plan saves your changes to the waves and their settings.
waves.html.nextStep: You can change a wave until it starts.

general.title: How this works, in short
points: Assess, accept, plan, run. An assessment changes nothing. A migration moves only the machines that an accepted assessment shows can migrate.
The product records each step of each machine, with its time and result.
A wave starts when a person starts it, or at its scheduled time. A wave can need an approval before it starts.
After you sign off the plan, the product starts each next wave when the wave before it ends. It waits while a machine waits for a person, or while the run is paused.
The product does not try to move a machine that cannot move. It shows the reason.
